t: For expenses of activities and agencies of the Department of Defense (other than the military departments) necessary for procurement, production, and modification of equipment, supplies, materials, and spare parts therefor, not otherwise provided for; the purchase of not to exceed 451 passenger motor vehicles, of which 447 shall be for replacement only; expansion of public and private plants, equipment, and installation thereof in such plants, erection of structures, and acquisition of land for the foregoing purposes, and such lands and interests therein, may be acquired, and construction prosecuted thereon prior to approval of title; reserve plant and Government and contractor-owned equipment layaway; $2,124,379,000, to remain available for obligation until September 30, 1998.

fable.w: This is an appropriations provision funding Defense-wide procurement, vehicle purchases, plant expansion and land acquisition. The tempting reading is that references to "private plants" and "contractor-owned equipment" bring outside parties in, but these only describe what the money may be spent on. Nothing requires or permits consultation, comment, hearings, advisory bodies, rulemaking or a right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government.
fable.s: expansion of public and private plants, equipment, and installation thereof in such plants

opus.w: This is a funding provision that lists what Department of Defense procurement money may be spent on. It sets up no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government. The mention of "private plants" only names something the funds may pay for; it does not bring private parties into a federal decision.
opus.s: expansion of public and private plants, equipment, and installation thereof in such plants, erection of structures, and acquisition of land for the foregoing purposes
opus.b:
This section only appropriates money, so it does not recommend or require participation.

The tempting reading is to treat "expansion of public and private plants" as involving private companies. That fails because it only describes what the money may be spent on. No outside party is consulted, coordinates with the government, comments, sits on an advisory body or gets a right to sue before a federal decision. Like Example 1, this is a funding provision.

qwen_chat.w: This section is an appropriations clause authorizing funds for specific Department of Defense activities, including procurement and construction. It does not establish any process for consulting with or coordinating with outside parties (such as the public, states, or private entities) before making a federal decision. The mention of 'private plants' refers to the location of construction or expansion, not to a participatory role for private owners in the decision-making process.
qwen_chat.s: For expenses of activities and agencies of the Department of Defense (other than the military departments) necessary for procurement, production, and modification of equipment, supplies, materials, and spare parts therefor, not otherwise provided for; the purchase of not to exceed 451 passenger motor vehicles, of which 447 shall be for replacement only; expansion of public and private plants, equipment, and installation thereof in such plants, erection of structures, and acquisition of land for the foregoing purposes, and such lands and interests therein, may be acquired, and construction prosecuted thereon prior to approval of title; reserve plant and Government and contractor-owned equipment layaway; $2,124,379,000, to remain available for obligation until September 30, 1998.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "expansion of public and private plants" implies coordination with private companies, thus constituting participation. However, this language describes the *scope* of procurement and construction activities funded by the appropriation, not a procedural requirement for the government to consult with or coordinate with outside parties before making a decision. The text is purely about funding authorization and allowable expenses.
